title: Blue Sheet (TP-00)
summary: The Blue Sheet sets the fair-comparison standard for Theophysics, defining two frameworks (Closed Naturalism vs. Theophysics) and the rules of engagement. It explicitly forbids hidden upgrades and subsidies, and states the burden of proof for Theophysics. The claims are mostly methodological and programmatic, with a central research proposal that shared triadic grammar may be grounded in God. No physics derivations or empirical predictions are made; the work is a bridge/meta document.

claims.claim_text: Every worldview must explain the same set of observations, including existence, distinction, lawfulness, information, measurement, consciousness, moral obligation, beauty, evil, guilt, love, sacrifice, repair, and hope.
evidence_needed: A defense that these are indeed the same observations for all worldviews.
evidence_present: The list of observations is stated as common data.
evidence_gap: No argument for why these specific items are the complete set or equally binding.
support: Every worldview has to explain the same world.
It has to explain: existence, distinction, lawfulness, information, measurement, consciousness, moral obligation, beauty, evil, guilt, love, sacrifice, repair, hope.
risks: The list may be contested; some items may be considered not universal.
claims.kill_condition: If a worldview can legitimately deny that some listed item is a real phenomenon to be explained.
claims.required_concession: The list is a proposed common ground, not an exhaustive or uncontested set.

claims.claim_text: The fair comparison between worldviews is based on coherence, explanatory power, assumption cost, register honesty, predictive/retrodictive reach, failure visibility, and human fit.
evidence_needed: A justification for these criteria as the correct standards.
evidence_present: The standards are listed as the same for both sides.
evidence_gap: No argument for why these criteria are the right ones or how they are weighted.
support: The comparison uses the same standards for both sides: Coherence, Explanatory power, Assumption cost, Register honesty, Predictive or retrodictive reach, Failure visibility, Human fit.
risks: Criteria may be vague or subjective; weighting is unspecified.
claims.kill_condition: If a worldview can reasonably reject these criteria as biased.
claims.required_concession: These criteria are proposed as fair but are not formally defined or weighted.

claims.claim_text: Closed Naturalism assumes that reality is ultimately impersonal and that mind, morality, meaning, love, truth, and religious experience must eventually be explained from below.
evidence_needed: A precise definition of Closed Naturalism and its commitments.
evidence_present: The framework is described as a broad alternative.
evidence_gap: No citation or formal definition; may be a straw man.
support: Framework A - Closed Naturalism: Reality is ultimately impersonal. Matter, energy, fields, laws, or physical information are the final floor. Mind, morality, meaning, love, truth, and religious experience must eventually be explained from below.
claims.kill_condition: If a naturalist can show that their view does not require explaining these from below.
claims.required_concession: This is a broad characterization for comparison, not a precise account of any specific naturalist theory.

claims.claim_text: Theophysics holds that reality is ultimately grounded in God, and that physics, information, consciousness, morality, meaning, and love are created-order witnesses at different resolutions.
evidence_needed: Theological support for the grounding claim and the witness metaphor.
evidence_present: The claim is stated as the framework's position.
evidence_gap: No specific theological sources are cited.
support: Framework B - Theophysics: Reality is ultimately grounded in God. Physics, information, consciousness, morality, meaning, and love are not separate territories with God added later. They are created-order witnesses at different resolutions.
risks: Theological claim without direct scriptural or traditional backing in this work.
claims.kill_condition: If the grounding claim is shown to be internally inconsistent or unsupported by Christian theology.
claims.required_concession: This is a stated premise, not a demonstrated conclusion.

claims.claim_text: The bridge between theology and physics is tested, not assumed.
evidence_needed: A method for testing the bridge.
evidence_present: The statement is made as a principle.
evidence_gap: No specific testing methodology is provided.
support: The bridge is tested, not assumed.
risks: Vague; could be used to claim testing without actual tests.
claims.kill_condition: If no concrete test is ever provided.
claims.required_concession: The testing method is not specified in this blue sheet.

claims.claim_text: Both frameworks must face the same data, including the intelligibility of the universe, the effectiveness of mathematics, the stability of physical laws, the reality of information, the existence of observers, first-person conscious experience, human perception of good and evil, non-random moral emotions, evil appearing parasitic on good, repair costing something, love commanding sacrifice against self-interest, and truth being treated as higher than error.
evidence_needed: A defense that these are indeed common data.
evidence_present: The list is stated as common data.
evidence_gap: No argument for why these are data rather than interpretations.
support: Both frameworks must face the same data: the universe is intelligible, mathematics works, physical laws are stable, information is real, observers exist, conscious experience is first-person, humans perceive good and evil, moral emotions are not randomly distributed, evil appears parasitic on good, repair costs something, love often commands sacrifice against self-interest, truth is treated as higher than error by every inquiry.
risks: Some items may be contested as data (e.g., moral emotions).
claims.kill_condition: If a framework can legitimately deny that some item is a datum.
claims.required_concession: These are proposed as common data, but their status as data is part of the debate.

claims.claim_text: Theophysics must not claim that physics proves God, that every scientific triad proves the Trinity, that every analogy is an isomorphism, that every emotional resonance is evidence, that every mathematical model is a theorem, or that every theological claim is a physics result.
evidence_needed: A commitment to avoid these overclaims.
support: Theophysics must not say: physics proves God, every scientific triad proves the Trinity, every analogy is an isomorphism, every emotional resonance is evidence, every mathematical model is a theorem, every theological claim is a physics result.
risks: These are self-imposed rules; may be violated in practice.
claims.kill_condition: If Theophysics violates these rules, it loses credibility.
claims.required_concession: These are stated as prohibitions, but compliance is not guaranteed.

claims.claim_text: Naturalism must not assume truth, lawfulness, consciousness, morality, meaning, or mathematical intelligibility without counting them as costs or explaining them without hidden subsidies.
evidence_needed: A demonstration that naturalism indeed makes these assumptions.
evidence_present: The prohibitions are stated as a challenge.
evidence_gap: No specific naturalist texts are cited.
support: Naturalism must not say: truth is assumed, but not counted as a cost; lawfulness is assumed, but not counted as a cost; consciousness is real when used, but reducible when explained; morality is binding in argument, but adaptive fiction in ontology; meaning is lived as real, but explained as illusion; mathematical intelligibility is just brute fact, while theology is accused of mystery.
risks: May be seen as a straw man.
claims.kill_condition: If a naturalist can show they do not make these assumptions.
claims.required_concession: This is a challenge to naturalism, not a demonstrated fact about all naturalist views.

claims.claim_text: Theophysics proposes that many apparently separate postulates (existence, distinction, relation, orientation, information, witness, coherence, moral order) may not be independent but may be projections of a deeper triadic ground.
evidence_needed: A research program to test this hypothesis.
evidence_present: The proposal is stated as the central research program.
evidence_gap: No evidence yet; it is a proposal.
support: Theophysics proposes that many apparently separate postulates may not be independent: existence, distinction, relation, orientation, information, witness, coherence, moral order. They may be projections of a deeper triadic ground.
claims.kill_condition: If the triadic ground is shown to be ad hoc or not explanatory.
claims.required_concession: This is a research proposal, not a demonstrated claim.

claims.claim_text: The created world repeatedly displays the same grammar: reality, relation, and witness; source, mediation, and record; state, transformation, and invariant.
evidence_needed: Examples of this grammar across domains.
evidence_present: The claim is stated as an observation.
evidence_gap: No specific examples are given in this work.
support: The created world repeatedly displays the same grammar: reality, relation, and witness; source, mediation, and record; state, transformation, and invariant.
risks: May be seen as vague or cherry-picked.
claims.kill_condition: If counterexamples are found where this grammar does not apply.
claims.required_concession: This is an assertion; examples are needed to support it.

claims.claim_text: The question of whether the repeated triadic grammar is accidental, emergent, brute, or grounded is open.
evidence_needed: Acknowledgment that this is an open question.
support: The question is whether that grammar is accidental, emergent, brute, or grounded.
claims.required_concession: This is an open question, not a claim.

claims.claim_text: If Theophysics is right, it must show three things: (1) the scientific, informational, conscious, and moral domains share real structure, not decorative similarity; (2) the shared structure reduces assumption cost rather than increasing it; (3) the Christian claim of a triune God uniquely grounds the structure without collapsing into monism, dualism, or arbitrary pluralism.
evidence_needed: A method to demonstrate each of these three requirements.
support: If Theophysics is right, it must show three things: The scientific, informational, conscious, and moral domains share real structure, not decorative similarity. The shared structure reduces assumption cost rather than increasing it. The Christian claim of a triune God uniquely grounds the structure without collapsing into monism, dualism, or arbitrary pluralism.
risks: The burden is high; failure to meet any one defeats the claim.
claims.kill_condition: If any of the three cannot be shown, Theophysics fails.
claims.required_concession: This is the burden of proof, not a claim of success.

claims.claim_text: Theophysics wins only if it explains more, hides less, and its bridges survive being named, graded, tested, and corrected.
support: Theophysics wins nothing by sounding more beautiful. It wins only if it explains more. It wins only if it hides less. It wins only if its bridges survive being named, graded, tested, and corrected.
risks: This is a self-imposed standard; may not be met.
claims.kill_condition: If Theophysics fails to meet this standard, it loses.
claims.required_concession: This is a standard, not a claim of achievement.

claims.claim_text: The blue-sheet rule is: Same observations. Same standards. No hidden upgrades. No hidden subsidies.
support: So the blue-sheet rule is: Same observations. Same standards. No hidden upgrades. No hidden subsidies.
claims.kill_condition: If the rule is not followed in practice.
claims.required_concession: This is a rule, not a description of actual practice.

claims.claim_text: Theophysics is the fair-comparison claim that Christian reality may explain the shared world with fewer hidden assumptions than closed naturalism, while preserving more of what humans and science both have to treat as real.
evidence_needed: A demonstration of fewer hidden assumptions and better preservation.
evidence_present: The claim is stated as the line to carry forward.
evidence_gap: No evidence is provided in this work.
support: Theophysics is the fair-comparison claim that Christian reality may explain the shared world with fewer hidden assumptions than closed naturalism, while preserving more of what humans and science both have to treat as real.
risks: This is a promissory claim; may be overclaimed if not demonstrated.
claims.kill_condition: If Theophysics cannot demonstrate fewer hidden assumptions or better preservation.
claims.required_concession: This is a claim to be tested, not a proven result.

fixes.problem: Closed Naturalism is defined broadly and may be a straw man.
fixes.repair: Add a footnote or reference to specific naturalist positions to avoid misrepresentation.

fixes.problem: The challenge to naturalism is stated without specific evidence.
fixes.repair: Provide examples or citations of naturalist arguments that make these assumptions.

fixes.problem: The claim of repeated triadic grammar is asserted without examples.
fixes.repair: Add examples from physics, information, consciousness, and morality to support the claim.

log_notes: The Blue Sheet is a methodological and programmatic document; it does not contain physics derivations or empirical predictions.
All claims are classified as ROOT because they are foundational premises or rules for the comparison.
The work explicitly forbids overclaims, which is a positive sign for the canon.
The central research program is the triadic grammar hypothesis, which is not yet demonstrated.
The burden of proof is clearly stated, which is a good practice.
